Criteria: Normal authentication and no bypass of first-login password change; reset returns the three requests to their baseline.
Expected Results: Support can complete the first-login control and reset returns REQ-SYN-001/002/003 with no Booking IDs, allocations, reservations or receiving records.

Automated test 'Demo reset baseline is repeatable and restores original requests, inventory, and empty downstream state' passed.

Description: Review the unassigned refrigerated shipment request and its ten intake categories.
Criteria: Request ID exists; source records and category extraction preserve the original conflicting evidence.
Expected Results: REQ-SYN-001 displays its own customer/source data, 2 x 40RF at 15 tonnes each, and the packing-list 40-tonne conflict.

Results: No authenticated browser interaction was possible. Automated tests passed: Ticket A retains original conflicting weight evidence and recalculates from complete clarification evidence; P1 detects Ticket A weight conflict and retains both original evidence values.

Test Scenario: Support / P1 — P1-03 assign and validate request
Description: Assign REQ-SYN-001, record the supported clarification, complete reviews and validate.
Criteria: Only Support can self-assign the Pending request; unresolved conflicts block validation; Request ID is not recreated.
Expected Results: Assigning changes Pending to Picked Up/In Progress and records audit. Clarification resolves only the weight conflict; validation becomes Ready for Submission after valid Support confirmation.

Results: No authenticated browser interaction was possible. Automated tests passed for Support self-assignment, conflict blocking, clarification-only recalculation, role-controlled review, and Request-ID gate.

Description: Verify the confirmed booking demand and evaluate current allocation options.
Criteria: Booking retains customer/Request ID, requires 2 x 40RF, and recommendations evaluate availability, readiness, capacity, cost and compatibility.

Test Scenario: Equipment Manager / P2 — P2-02 approval, reservation and persistence
Description: Approve a feasible recommendation using the card-level approval control and re-open the POC.
Criteria: Approval requires a justification and Equipment Manager permission; only one reservation/approval persists; a draft Operations instruction remains separate.
Expected Results: Selected option becomes Approved, reserves the required containers once, records draft instruction/history, and remains Approved after refresh/login.
Test Steps: Enter justification on feasible Option A; select Approve Allocation; inspect inventory/history/instruction; refresh; log out/in and re-open the booking.
Results: No authenticated browser interaction was possible. Automated tests passed for incompatible allocation blocking, compatible reservation, double-allocation prevention, and allocation-history search. Persistence/refresh and duplicate-record observations remain unexecuted in browser.

Test Scenario: Equipment Manager / P2 — P2-03 execution-to-receiving journey transition
Description: Investigate how an authorized P2 execution update moves the shared booking journey to receiving eligibility.
Criteria: Execution status must remain distinct from the booking journey; no arrival may be fabricated. A real, authorized existing transition is required before P3 accepts the booking.
Expected Results: If a transition exists, it records the allowed journey event and P3 makes the booking eligible; otherwise the test records the exact missing transition.
Test Steps: After P2-02, change the approved allocation execution status through existing P2 controls, including Completed; inspect booking journey in P2 and then Receiving & Handoff.
Results: Blocked before browser execution by first-login control. Static implementation inspection verified that the P2 control updates only allocation execution status; the booking remains Equipment Allocation. P3 eligibility expressly excludes Equipment Allocation and admits Arrived at Receiving Location or later. No existing authorized UI control advances this transition.

Test Scenario: Equipment Manager / P2 — P2-04 duplicate/reversion investigation
Description: Investigate duplicate approvals, duplicate reservations/modification history, and Approved reverting after refresh/login.
Criteria: Each current option appears once; one approval creates one reservation; Approved remains Approved across refresh/login.
Expected Results: No duplicate approval/reservation/history records and no Approved-to-Draft/Pending reversion occur.
Test Steps: Perform P2-02 once; recalculate/select/edit only one option; inspect current cards and history; refresh; log out/in; compare reservation and approval records.
Results: Not executed because normal authenticated P2 access was blocked. Existing automated tests only confirm double-allocation prevention and history search; they do not provide browser proof for duplicates or persistence.

Test Scenario: Receiver / P3 — P3-01 receiving workload eligibility
Description: Verify the Receiver workload contains the same booking only after the shared journey reaches receiving.
Criteria: A booking in Equipment Allocation is excluded; arrival or later makes it eligible without fabricating progress.
Expected Results: The generated booking is unavailable until Arrived at Receiving Location; it becomes selectable at an eligible existing journey state.
Test Steps: After P2-03 achieves a legitimate arrival state, log out; log in as Harper Receiver; open Receiving & Handoff; inspect the eligible list.
Results: Blocked because P2-03 has no existing authorized arrival transition and normal login could not be completed. Automated test passed that Equipment Allocation/Ocean Transit are excluded while Arrived at Receiving Location and later are eligible.

Test Scenario: Receiver / P3 — P3-02 receiving, discrepancy and handoff gates
Description: Perform physical checks, inspect evidence comparison, resolve a genuine discrepancy and approve handoff.
Criteria: Receiver permission is required; physical validation, manual discrepancy resolution and approval gates remain human-controlled.
Expected Results: The booking moves to Under Validation then Handed Off only after the required evidence and Receiver approval; history stays under the same Booking ID.
Test Steps: With an eligible booking, select it; record physical cargo checks; inspect documents; resolve a valid discrepancy if present; select Approve handoff; inspect journey/history.
Results: Not executed because receiving eligibility and authentication were blocked. Automated tests passed for checklist/comparison, human evidence requirements, handoff blocking before gates, and structured multi-transfer history.

Test Scenario: Receiver / P3 — P3-03 POD and delivery completion
Description: Record POD and Receiver confirmation after all receiving gates.
Criteria: POD must be present and linked to the Booking ID; completion is blocked without POD, resolved discrepancy, approval and zero outstanding quantity.
Expected Results: POD displays Present; Receiver confirmation is recorded; journey becomes Delivered / Completed and delivery summary is available.
Test Steps: After P3-02, select Record POD and confirm delivery; inspect document comparison, journey and final delivery summary; attempt same action before satisfying a gate as a negative check.
Results: Not executed because receiving eligibility and authentication were blocked. Automated tests passed that equal expected/received quantities reconcile, POD becomes present only after valid gates, and delivery remains blocked until required evidence/approval/POD/quantity conditions pass.

Description: Verify completed approved allocations appear in the Receiver-only arrival worklist without being treated as arrived automatically.
Criteria: An approved plan with execution Completed and journey Equipment Allocation is awaiting arrival; only a Receiver or Administrator may confirm arrival; confirmation moves the booking to the existing Arrived at Receiving Location status.
Expected Results: Completed execution alone does not make the booking receiving-eligible. Receiver confirmation adds a shared booking-history event and makes it available to the normal receiving list.
Test Steps: Create/approve a booking allocation; set execution to Completed; log in as Harper Receiver; open Receiving & Handoff; select Confirm Arrival; inspect the shared booking in P1/P2/P3.
Results: Automated rule test passed: a completed Approved allocation is awaiting arrival while still excluded from receiving; In Progress and already-arrived bookings are excluded. Browser interaction is blocked at the user-controlled first-login password-change submission, so button permission, visible move and cross-module UI update are not claimed.
